evidence.curator_note: adduct corrected to null (convention G): the species undergoing this reaction is an EVEN-ELECTRON cation (charge +1, radical_electrons 0) - a fragment/secondary-fragmentation precursor - NOT the [M]+. radical molecular ion. Eq 8.1, consecutive dissociation of the top pathway: the C4H7+ (1-methylallyl) cation, arrow labeled 'rH' (rate 2.5), loses neutral CH4 to give C3H3+ (dHf/IE 11.1(6.6)) + CH4 (dHf -0.8). This is the C4H7+ -> C3H3+ + CH4 step the running text on this page calls out explicitly. Book draws 0 curved arcs (net summary equation). Mechanism reconstructed for electron balance: the methyl (C5) departs as CH4, taking a hydrogen from the vinyl terminus (C2), and the three surviving carbons close to the aromatic cyclopropenyl cation. Two curved (2-electron) arrows carry the heavy-atom skeleton: (1) the C2=C3 pi electrons shift to form the new C3=C4 pi bond, (2) the C4-C5 sigma bond's electrons close the C2-C4 ring bond while methyl leaves. The accompanying H transfer C2->C5 (which completes CH4) cannot be atom-mapped -- RDKit folds mapped explicit H into implicit valence -- so it appears only as the H-count change written into the SMILES (C2: =CH2 -> ring =CH; C5: CH3 -> CH4) and is not carried by an explicit arrow; the two encoded arrows already reproduce every heavy-atom bond-order change exactly. The charge relocates C4 -> C2 as drawn (aromatic cyclopropenyl cation).

[H]7[C]8([H]9)([H]10)([H]11)' performs the SAME net transformation: it closes an aromatic three-membered cyclopropenyl cation (the ':1' ring over their C1/C3/C5) and expels CH4 (their C8 plus the migrated H7). CONNECTIVITY MATCHES. Representation differences: the MOD rule writes the product ring with aromatic bonds (':') whereas this record uses a RDKit-valid Kekule form ([CH+]1[CH]=[CH]1), and the MOD rule (being a term graph) can atom-map the migrating H while this JSON record cannot.

Book prints '(35%)' adjacent to the C3H3+ + CH4 products of this branch. observed_mz 39.0229 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of C3H3+ (m/z 39). Note the same m/z 39 ion is also produced by the middle pathway's H2-loss step (C3H5+ -> C3H3+ + H2); the printed (35%) is the C3H3+ abundance, its channel split not resolved on the page.
